survey: A cowboy lasso (lariat), seen roughly face-on and lying flat. On the left is a coil of rope made of about four or five stacked wraps, drawn as offset rings so the coil looks like a crescent. A red cord is tied around the top of the coil, with two cut ends sticking up. A straight tail drops from the bottom front of the coil and ends in a cream whipped cap. On the right, a second strand leaves the coil at its lower right and runs to a cream honda ring (the small eye a lasso loop slides through). From the honda, a large open loop (the noose) swings out to the right. The rope is one continuous piece, the coil is held by the tie, and the noose runs through the honda, so overall the object reads as a working lasso.

errors.where: Honda ring between the coil and the big loop
errors.what: The honda is drawn as a plain bead with rope passing through it on both sides. No rope end is tied or spliced into it. In a real lasso the end of the rope is fixed at the honda and the rope runs through it to make the noose. Here the noose looks like a closed ring threaded onto a bead, so it is unclear how the loop could be pulled tight.

errors.where: Point where the hanging tail leaves the bottom front of the coil
errors.what: The tail bends straight out of the front wrap and seems to merge into the coil, instead of clearly being the last turn coming off the coil. The coil's inner wraps also stack into a crescent rather than reading as separate round turns.

fix: Show the honda as a small rope eye or a ring spliced onto the end of the rope. Have the rope's end clearly tied into the honda, and have the other part of the rope slide through it to form the noose, then run back to the coil. Draw the coil as separate, evenly round wraps, and have the hanging tail clearly peel off the outermost wrap before ending in the whipped cap.
